chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunting of the Magians for fish when they strike with the net and do not recite the name of God, or a Jew and he does not recite the name. He said, 'There is no harm; indeed, the hunting of fish is merely catching them.'

key_terms.وَ لاَ يُسَمُّونَ: And they do not recite the name (of God)

ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by non-Muslims who do not say Bismillah permissible to eat?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the ritual requirement of *tasmiyah* (reciting God's name) applies to land animals but not to fish, as their capture is considered a form of slaughter in itself. This ruling extends to non-Muslims (Ahl al-Kitab and Magians), establishing that their method of catching fish is sufficient for permissibility regardless of whether they invoke God's name, highlighting the distinct jurisprudential category of aquatic life in Shia fiqh. This principle underscores the ease (*rukhsah*) granted regarding seafood, distinguishing it from the stricter conditions applied to terrestrial game.
